svg.text: Carrier 24ABC6 — how it’s wired
A beginner-friendly map of the real parts and how the wires connect them. The real manual is one tap away.
HIGH VOLTAGE · 240V
— the power that actually runs the compressor & fan
LOW VOLTAGE · 24V
— the small signal from inside that switches it on
WHAT THE LETTERS MEAN
L1 / L2
the two 240-volt power legs coming in
T1 / T2
power leaving the contactor to the parts
C · R · S
compressor terminals: Common / Run / Start
HERM
capacitor → compressor (short for “hermetic”)
FAN
capacitor → the outdoor fan motor
“C” = Common in every spot — but it’s a different wire each place.

g.text: the switch that powers the unit on

svg.text: WHAT EACH WIRE DOES
find a wire’s number ⓘ on the drawing, then read it here · ● = wires joined
One leg of the 240-volt power to the contactor.
Power from contactor to the compressor common terminal.
Start winding of compressor to the run capacitor.
Compressor run terminal to the capacitor common spade.
Capacitor fan terminal to the outdoor fan motor.
Power leg to the outdoor fan motor.
24-volt "turn on" signal from indoors to the contactor coil
24-volt common back to the indoor unit
